summary: v135.38 unified template hub (/sablonlar) tested end-to-end. Backend: 19 pytest cases across /api/rsvp-templates (CRUD + archive + send), /api/event-templates (full PATCH + archive filter) and /api/telegram-templates (archived default + PATCH archived) — 18 pass, 1 fails and exposes a CRITICAL targeting bug in the RSVP send endpoint. Frontend: full Playwright coverage of all 3 tabs (Telegram / Etkinlik / RSVP Hatırlatma) — create, edit(PATCH), archive→Arşiv tab→Geri Getir restore, delete, RSVP send modal with event picker + 'Belki dahil', plus regression on the old /admin/telegram-sablonlar route and the header 'Şablonlar' menu item. All UI flows passed. All test data cleaned up; pre-existing 'T1' event template preserved.

critical.issue: Targeting query is wrong: it filters `db.users` by `alliance_name` and reads `users.telegram_chat_id`, but the users collection has NEITHER field (verified: users keys = id, username, email, role, can_edit, member_ids, must_change_password, created_at). Alliance + telegram_chat_id live on `db.members`, resolved via user.member_ids / user.member_id / members.user_id (see server.py `_resolve_user_alliances`). Result: for ANY event with alliance_scope set (every real event defaults to 'GOW') target_count is ALWAYS 0 — the feature silently sends nothing. Proof: event 'L2' (scope='GOW', 0 RSVP rows, 9 users linked to GOW members) -> target_count=0; unscoped event 'Kafes 2' -> target_count=10. Telegram DM will also never fire because telegram_chat_id is only on members.

minor.issue: alliance_scope == 'all' is treated as a literal alliance name (only empty string means everyone), unlike server.py `_rsvp_alliance_query` which treats 'all'/empty as no filter -> 0 targets for 'all'-scoped events.
Does not honour per-channel push opt-out (`_users_disabled_for_pref('reminder')`) that every other push fanout in server.py applies; opted-out users will still receive these pushes.
send_count is incremented / last_sent_at stamped even when target_count==0 and nothing was delivered — inflates the '1 gönderim' badge shown in the UI.
Push branch (pywebpush + lazy `from server import _get_or_create_vapid`) could NOT be exercised: db.push_subscriptions is empty in this environment, so the loop is skipped. Untested code path.
Returns HTTP 200, not 201, for creation (spec said '201-ish'); also user filter `is_active: {$ne: False}` relies on a field absent from users docs (harmless today, silently no-op).

integration_issues.issue: UI wiring is correct (event picker populated with 8 events, submit disabled until an event is picked, toast rendered: '0 üyeye gönderildi (Push 0 / Telegram 0)', send_count badge updated to '1 gönderim'), but because of the backend targeting bug the toast always reports 0 members for alliance-scoped events, so admins get a false 'success'.

issues: Info hint banner (text-[11px] text-muted-foreground on rgba(56,189,248,0.08) background) is very low contrast and visually cramped against its 1px border — barely legible at 1920px; bump to text-sky-200/text-xs with more padding.

React hydration warning on the RSVP send modal: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — the event <option> renders {e.name} through the preview instrumentation wrapper. Cosmetic/dev-only, but noisy; consider passing a plain string label.

action_items: CRITICAL: rewrite the target resolution in /app/backend/routes/rsvp_templates.py to resolve alliance + telegram_chat_id via the users->members join (reuse server.py `_resolve_user_alliances` / members.telegram_chat_id) instead of users.alliance_name / users.telegram_chat_id; treat alliance_scope 'all'/empty as everyone.
Honour `_users_disabled_for_pref('reminder')` opt-out in the RSVP push fanout.
Only bump send_count/last_sent_at when target_count > 0 (or surface a warning toast when 0 targets).
Improve contrast/padding of the RSVP hint banner on /sablonlar.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: /app/backend/routes/rsvp_templates.py builds its candidate query as {'is_active': {'$ne': False}, 'alliance_name': event.alliance_scope} against db.users. In this app the users collection stores only auth/link data (member_ids) — alliance_name and telegram_chat_id live on db.members, and the canonical resolution path is server.py `_resolve_user_alliances()` (user.member_ids + user.member_id + reverse members.user_id -> members.alliance_name, case-sensitive: GOW != GoW != GOw). Reproduction: POST /api/rsvp-templates then POST /api/rsvp-templates/{id}/send {event_id: <GOW-scoped event>, include_maybe:false} -> 200 with target_count 0, while the same call on an event without alliance_scope returns target_count 10. Mitigation: resolve the user->member->alliance map (batched) and pull telegram_chat_id from the linked member docs; treat scope ''/'all' as all users.
